stories.body: Sean dropped 189.14 on Tim, the best score of Week 9, while Marissa upset Hogies 107.98–102.30. That leaves Sean and Hogies tied at 7–2, and Sean takes the top seed on points, 1,327.3 to 1,185.0.
stories.headline: Sean is the new No. 1 seed
Oscar’s Week 8 predictions are live
stories.body: Zach and Baby Abdo meet in the Game of the Week, Hogies and Bob play for first place, and Tyler faces the players he traded to Sean. Plus Oscar’s 12-leg TD parlay, with Jahmyr Gibbs as the golden leg.

stories.historic: First three-team trade in league history
stories.headline: History made: the first three-team trade
stories.body: Tyler, Tyriese and Shmoody just swapped 11 players in the first three-team trade in Villains history. Tyler lands Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams, Shmoody gets Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry, and Tyriese walks away with five starters including James Cook, D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins.

stories.headline: Oscar’s Week 9 predictions are live
stories.body: Zach and Mo climb the ladder for the Smoke Boy Championship in the Game of the Week, Hogies hunts Marissa, and Tyriese and Shmoody settle the three-team trade. Plus Oscar’s 12-leg TD parlay, with Jahmyr Gibbs as the golden leg again.

stories.headline: The Week 9 recap is here
stories.body: Mo wins a Monday night Mortal Kombat match for the belt, Sean posterizes Tim with 189 points, and Tyriese beats Shmoody by 0.04 in the closest game in league history. Plus manager news, Oscar's 4-for-12 parlay and new power rankings.

stories.headline: Power rankings: Sean takes the throne
stories.body: Sean moves to No. 1 after the second-highest score of the season. Hogies slips to second after trading away McCaffrey, Bob climbs to third, and Abdo jumps two spots after springing his trap on Tyler.

trades.headline: Tyler sells Jeremiyah Love for the Vikings backfield

sides.note: Tyler sent Jeremiyah Love (RB23, on injured reserve), Zonovan Knight (out) and $25 of FAAB to the Trade God for Aaron Jones Sr. (RB37) and Jordan Mason (RB41), the whole Vikings backfield. At 3–6 he needs backs who play on Sunday, and he got two. He paid with the most valuable piece in the deal, which is the usual price of urgency.

The Trade God takes on two injured backs, collects $25 for the trouble and comes out about 29% ahead. Love has the highest market value in the deal, and injured reserve is not forever. Patience is a virtue, particularly when someone else is paying for it.

Hogies sent Christian McCaffrey (RB4) and Kaelon Black to Baby Abdo for Josh Jacobs (RB16) and George Pickens (WR19), about 16% less value by the numbers. Sitting alone in first, he has chosen two starters over one star. Depth is what one calls it once the headliner has left.

Baby Abdo lands McCaffrey, still a top-five back, plus his handcuff Kaelon Black, and comes out about 16% ahead. He gives up two starters to do it, but stars win weeks and weeks win playoff spots. It is always pleasant to buy the best thing in the shop.

trades.headline: Tyler sends Bowers to Sean for Jonathan Taylor

sides.note: Tyler sent Brock Bowers (TE1) and Javonte Williams (RB8) to seanwavy for Jonathan Taylor (RB5) and rookie Jonah Coleman, about 25% less value, ten days after landing both in the three-team trade. Taylor has the highest market value in the deal, but the best tight end in the league is the harder thing to replace. One should never trade a rarity for a commodity, however handsome the commodity.

seanwavy adds the league's top tight end and a starting back and comes out about 25% ahead. He already scores more points than anyone in the league, and now he has the one position nobody else can fill. The rich, as ever, get Bowers.
Collin trades A.J. Brown (WR18) for Jameson Williams (WR26), who scored 14 points a game in Detroit before this. The cheaper of the two, which is not usually what one shops for.
Baby Abdo gets the bigger name and the bigger value. Brown has only 6.4 points a game in New England, so this is a bet on a reputation. Reputations, unlike receivers, rarely pull a hamstring.

trades.headline: History: the first three-team trade
trades.historic: First three-team trade in league history

sides.note: Tyler sent three players (James Cook, Jalen Coker and Kyle Monangai) and came back with two better ones: Brock Bowers, the TE2, and Javonte Williams, the RB9. Consolidation is the only form of subtraction that makes a man richer, and an elite tight end is the rarest thing in this league.

Tyriese gave up the best player in the deal, Puka Nacua, but came away with five starters: Cook, Swift and Higgins fill his lineup, and Coker gives him cover. One injury no longer wrecks his week, and when Mike Evans returns he will have one of the deepest benches in the league. Quantity has its own quality.

Shmoody took the prize of the deal, Puka Nacua (WR2), plus Derrick Henry, five days after acquiring Swift and Higgins and immediately spending them. Going from Bowers to LaPorta at tight end is the price of the jewel, and at 1–6 he can no longer afford to be patient.
Collin sends DeVonta Smith (WR20, 17.2 a game) away for Josh Downs and $55 of FAAB. FAAB is lovely in December, but in October it does not score.
Tyriese adds a third WR1-type to his new depth chart for a bench piece and some loose change. Smith is questionable this week, which is the only fine print.
Collin turns a waiver-wire quarterback into $8 of free FAAB. Free money is the only kind that never disappoints.
Tyriese paid $8 for Kyler Murray and released him 25 seconds later. Whatever this was, it was not about Kyler.

cover.headline: The League Is at War
cover.dek: Twelve teams, one battlefield. The three-team trade debuts, Hogies and Bob fight for first, Tyler faces his old players and two teams claw their way out of the Toilet Bowl. Week 8 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.

games.title: Zach vs. Baby Abdo: Can Abdo Beat His Old Amon-Ra?
games.lineText: (5–2) Zach - Trade God (−130) vs. (3–4) Abdo - Beat the case (+110)
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −3.5 | Total: 254 | Projection: Zach 128.9 - Abdo 125.2
story: Two weeks ago, Abdo traded Amon-Ra St. Brown to Tyler. Tyler flipped him to Zach a week later. On Sunday, Abdo finally sees him again, wearing the wrong jersey. Amon-Ra is questionable, and Abdo is hoping it stays that way.

Zach is 5–2 and has won his last two, including Sean's profile picture. His playoff odds are 94%. The Trade God has made more deals than anyone except Tyler, and most of them have worked. Bijan Robinson is projected for 21, Amon-Ra and Luther Burden, both from the Tyler blockbuster, give him a pair of starting receivers, and Dallas Goedert holds down tight end. Since Zach puts a deal together every week, the lineup will probably look different again by Sunday.

Abdo is 3–4, and his playoff odds are 15%. He has won two straight and has been building all season: Bucky Irving, George Pickens and DK Metcalf from Tyler, and A.J. Brown last night for Jameson Williams. Omar Cooper Jr. is averaging 22.5 a game. Lamar Jackson is questionable, but Jordan Love is on the bench in case the baby needs a babysitter. A loss puts him at 3–5, and at that point the playoffs are mostly a rumor.
The last two times these two met, they split. Zach won 138.84–106.62 in Week 2 last year, and Abdo got him back 124.24–110.04 in Week 13. The fans like Abdo 4–1. The sportsbook doesn't.

watch.text: The best projection in the game and the reason the Trade God is favored.
Questionable. If he plays, the baby has a chance. If he doesn't, Jordan Love babysits.

locker: Zach
I collect players. Abdo gave one away. Sunday I'll explain why that was a mistake.
Abdo
Amon-Ra knows what he did. Mo set the record against me. Shmoody lost to me. Zach is next.
games.oscarNote: Oscar is picking against the fans and siding with the man who has Bijan. If Amon-Ra sits, Oscar reserves the right to deny he ever said so.

games.title: Hogies vs. Sgt. Bob: Who Owns First Place?
games.lineText: (6–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (+180) vs. (5–2) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−220)
games.spreadText: Spread: Bob −14 | Total: 212.5 | Adjusted Projection: Bob 128.7 - Hogies 114 (with Hogies' bye-week replacements)
story: First place is on the line. Hogies is alone at the top at 6–1 and has won three straight. Bob is a game back at 5–2. He has also scored 982 points to Hogies' 980, so the man in first is chasing the man with the better team on paper. If Hogies wins, he goes to 7–1 and opens up a two-game lead. If Bob wins, they're both 6–2, and Bob takes first on points.

Hogies has picked a bad week to lose half his lineup to byes. Christian McCaffrey, Chris Olave, Jaylin Noel and Jordan Watkins all have the week off, and so do most of the players on his bench. He'll be shopping on the waiver wire by Sunday. What he has left is good, though. Dak Prescott is projected for 22.7, Trey McBride is the best tight end in the league that doesn't belong to Tyler, and Chuba Hubbard has quietly averaged 18 a game. The student has become a teacher in the standings, but this week he's a substitute teacher.

Bob has Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is averaging 28 points a game and is the most dangerous receiver in the league. Kyren Williams adds 19.6 a game, and Drake London and Denzel Boston fill out a receiving room that would make most teams jealous. The only question mark is at quarterback, where Malik Willis is starting and hasn't played a down for him yet.
Bob has owned this matchup. He beat Hogies 166.94–91.14 in Week 6 last year and won again in Week 15, 141.68–132.48. The fans like Bob 4–1.

watch.text: With four starters on bye, the tight end has to play like a wide receiver and a running back at once.
28 points a game. The most dangerous receiver in the league, and Hogies has nobody to match him.

locker: Hogies
Byes don't scare me. I've been winning with backups all year. Bob's points don't count on the standings page.
Bob
Enjoy the view from first place, Hogies. It's about to be a lot shorter.
games.oscarNote: First place is a lovely address, but Hogies is only renting it. Bob has the lease, the furniture and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

games.title: Tyler vs. Sean: Can Tyler Beat His Old Team?
games.lineText: (3–4) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (+405) vs. (5–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−555)
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −30 | Total: 250.5 | Adjusted Projection: Sean 140.9 - Tyler 122.4 (line set before the three-team trade)
story: Sean's team is named after CeeDee Lamb, and Tyler is the one who traded him there. Before Week 1, Tyler sent CeeDee to Sean for Kenneth Walker. A week later, he sent Walker to Sean too. On Sunday, Tyler faces the two best players he's ever traded away, both wearing the same jersey. Walker is averaging 24.6 a game and CeeDee 22.2. Zay Flowers went to Sean and came back, and Joe Burrow arrived from Zach. Half of Sean's team has a receipt with Tyler's name on it.

Tyler is 3–4, has lost two straight and has lost on the final play three times this season. His playoff odds were 25% before Tuesday night, when he made the first three-team trade in league history to land Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams. With Williams, Flowers and Bowers, Tyler finally has the firepower to match Sean's big three. Jared Goff runs the offense, and Makai Lemon and Antonio Williams are his flex plays. The questions are Ladd McConkey and Jeremiyah Love, who are both questionable. The sportsbook set this line before the trade, which is why it reads like an insult.

Sean has scored 998 points, the most in the league, and he's 5–2 even after losing his profile picture to Zach last week. His big three are Walker, CeeDee and Joe Burrow, and Jonathan Taylor makes them a big four. His only soft spots are DJ Moore and Zach Charbonnet, who are both questionable.
Tyler has the history on his side. He beat Sean twice last year, 154.08–98.84 in Week 1 and 123.22–99.94 in Week 12. The fans like Sean 4–1.

watch.text: The prize of the three-team trade makes his debut. Tyler needs him to play like the TE1 on day one.
Averaging 24.6 a game since Tyler sent him over. Every point is a reminder.

locker: Tyler
Sean doesn't have a team. He has my old team. I know every one of those guys' weaknesses.
Sean
Thanks for CeeDee. Thanks for Walker. Thanks in advance for the win.
games.oscarNote: Tyler built a better team this week, but Sean built his out of Tyler's old one. Oscar is sad to report that the original still beats the remake.

games.title: Tyriese vs. Mo: Can Depth Beat the Beast?
games.lineText: (3–4) Tyriese - Welcome to Loveland 🫶 (+180) vs. (3–4) Mo - Beazy (−220)
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −14 | Total: 258 | Adjusted Projection: Mo 139.5 - Tyriese 122.6
story: Both are 3–4, and the winner reaches .500. Mohammed holds the sixth playoff spot on points, and Tyriese sits just behind him. A loss doesn't end anyone's season, but it does start the countdown.

Tyriese spent Tuesday night rebuilding his roster. In four trades, he added James Cook, D'Andre Swift, Tee Higgins, Jalen Coker and DeVonta Smith, and briefly Kyler Murray, for about 25 seconds. This is the debut of the new Loveland. Caleb Williams leads it, Cook and Swift share the backfield, and Higgins, Coker and Stefon Diggs make up the receivers. The team runs five deep at receiver and running back. What it doesn't have anymore is Puka Nacua, and on a big week, a superstar wins games that depth can't.

Mohammed has won three straight and is the hottest team in the league. He set the league record with 196.10 against Abdo and has gone 3–0 since. Josh Allen is back from his bye, and Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are both healthy. Both of those receivers came over in trades, and Jefferson came from Tyler. Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are on bye, but his bench covers both spots. At full strength, this might be the most talented team in the league, and he's no longer playing without a quarterback.
Last year, Tyriese beat Mohammed 179.12–130.68 in Week 4. The fans like Mohammed 4–1.

watch.text: His third team in a week. Tyriese gave up Puka to get him, so he'd better feel at home fast.
Back from the bye. Last week Mo had no quarterback; this week he has the best one in the game.

locker: Tyriese
Mo has three stars. I have ten starters. Do the math.
Mo
I set the record without a quarterback. Now I have one. Welcome to Loveland? Welcome to the beast.
games.oscarNote: Depth is a comfort in October, but stars win in November. Mohammed has three, and Tyriese traded his only one away on Tuesday.

games.title: Collin vs. Tim: Can the Annoyance Survive the Coffey Shop?
games.lineText: (3–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+165) vs. (4–3) Tim - The Coffey Shop (−200)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tim −12 | Total: 264.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tim 139.8 - Collin 118.9
story: This is the new guys' game. Collin took over Jordan's team this year, and Tim took over Ryan's. Neither has had a full season to earn a reputation, and both have spent this one making a name in the trade market. Tim is 4–3 with playoff odds of 74%. Collin is 3–4 at 36%, and a loss would make it feel a lot lower.

Collin has been the league's busiest trader after Tyler, and on Tuesday night he made three more deals. He added Jameson Williams and Josh Downs, plus $63 in FAAB. Last week Jahmyr Gibbs sat on his bench. This week Gibbs starts, and at 28.5 points a game he's the best running back in the league. Kirk Cousins has averaged 18.8 since arriving, Tony Pollard is steady, and Germie Bernard has quietly put up 15.7 a game. Breece Hall is questionable again. Collin has also been unlucky: 975 points have been scored against him, the second-most in the league. He's a better team than his record says.

Tim's best move came in Week 4, when he got Bo Nix and $100 of FAAB for Patrick Mahomes. Since then, he's built a deep, balanced team. Trevor Lawrence is projected for 21.4, Ashton Jeanty and Chase Brown share the backfield, and Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Parker Washington are all averaging more than 15 a game. His one weak spot is at tight end, where Kyle Pitts is averaging 5.7 points a game. Golden and Jaylen Waddle are both questionable.
These two have never played each other. The fans like Tim 4–1.

watch.text: 28.5 a game and out of the lineup last week. Collin will not make that mistake twice.
The engine of the Coffey Shop. If he gets going early, Collin's comeback math stops working.

locker: Collin
They call me the annoyance of the league. Tim's about to find out why.
Tim
I took Mahomes out of my lineup and got better. Imagine what I'll do to Collin.
games.oscarNote: Collin has the best player on the field and the worst luck in the league. On Sunday, Oscar expects the luck to win.

games.title: Marissa vs. Shmoody: Who Gets Off the Bus?
games.lineText: (1–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (−220) vs. (1–6) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (+180)
games.spreadText: Spread: Marissa −13.5 | Total: 253.5 | Adjusted Projection: Marissa 134.0 - Shmoody 116 (line set before the three-team trade)
story: The two 1–6 teams play for the right to not be alone in last place. The loser falls to 1–7. The winner escapes the basement, at least for a week. Both are down to playoff odds of 2% and 4%, and the sportsbook makes them the top two favorites for the Toilet Bowl.

Last year, Shmoody won the whole league. Now he's 1–6, has lost three games by less than a touchdown, and has had enough of waiting. Over five days, he traded for D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins, then sent them away again to land Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry in the three-team trade. Both debut on Sunday. Geno Smith is averaging 23.5 a game, more than almost any quarterback in the league. The rest of the lineup is the problem: Blake Corum, Rome Odunze and Ja'Kobi Lane aren't scaring anyone. The sportsbook set this line before the trade, so it still prices Shmoody without Puka.

Marissa has scored 807 points, the fewest in the league, and 1,005 have been scored against her, the most. Some of that is her team and some of it is bad luck. Drake Maye has been solid, Tetairoa McMillan is averaging 16.2, and Bhayshul Tuten, her team's namesake, is averaging 14.7. The other half of the name has been the problem: Saquon Barkley is averaging 7.6 a game and is questionable again. She also has Patrick Mahomes sitting on her bench, which is a sentence that should never apply to a 1–6 team.
Last year Marissa beat Shmoody 111.24–106.20 in Week 11. The fans like Shmoody 4–1.

watch.text: He has run in a touchdown two weeks straight. Marissa needs a third.
The prize of the three-team trade debuts. The champion is betting the season on him.

locker: Marissa
Everybody keeps scoring 160 on me. Shmoody doesn't have 160 in him.
Shmoody
I'm still the champion. Puka just got here. The basement is for Marissa.
games.oscarNote: The fans believe in the champion and Oscar respects the sentiment. But Marissa has the better lineup, and Shmoody has the better excuses.

parlay.headline: Twelve legs, three debuts, one golden boy
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in.
picks: 28.5 points a game and finally back in the lineup. The surest thing on the slip.
The Trade God's one untouchable. Atlanta gives him the ball at the goal line.
Green Bay's goal-line back. Abdo needs a touchdown more than anyone in the Game of the Week.
Bob's touchdown machine near the end zone, and a safer bet than JSN to find paydirt.
With McCaffrey on bye, Hogies' backfield belongs to him.
Day one of the three-team era. Dallas's lead back should get the short ones.
Two touchdowns the last time Oscar picked him. Tyler would prefer he forget how.
Third team in a week, same end zone. Buffalo always finds him there.
Back from the bye and the best running quarterback in the league. Oscar has learned this lesson before.
Oscar missed on him in Week 5. Oscar does not hold grudges, only parlay slips.
Two straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Oscar is going for three.
The champion's new back is 32 years old and has never once been stopped at the 1-yard line.
parlay.sign: Gibbs is the golden leg. Josh Allen is the danger leg, because Oscar's quarterback picks have gone 3-for-6. If all twelve cash, Oscar retires to the countryside.

cover.headline: The League's Judgment Day
cover.dek: The league is running out of excuses. Zach and Mo climb the ladder for the Smoke Boy belt, Hogies hunts from first place, Tyriese and Shmoody settle the three-team trade, and Tyler and Abdo fight for their playoff lives. Week 9 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.

games.title: Zach vs. Mo: Who Climbs the Ladder for the Smoke Boy Championship?
games.lineText: (6–2) Zach - Trade God (−135) vs. (3–5) Mo - Beazy (+110)
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −4 | Total: 285.5 | Projection: Zach 144.8 - Mo 140.6
story: The belt hangs over the ring and both men are on the ladder. The Smoke Boy Championship goes to whoever reaches it first, and the 285.5-point total is the highest of the week, so the sportsbook expects fireworks.

Zach is 6–2 and has won three straight, including a 126.28–84.90 win over Baby Abdo last week. His playoff odds are 99%. He's also the luckiest team in the league: only 897.5 points have been scored against him, the fewest of any team. Bijan Robinson leads the league's best backfield with 153 points and is projected for 23.2 this week. Amon-Ra St. Brown has 141 and is questionable. Jayden Daniels is projected for 18.6 at quarterback, and George Kittle is back from his bye at tight end. The Trade God has found a way every week, and the record shows it.

Mo is 3–5, which makes no sense. He has scored 1,125 points, the second-most in the league, and has had the second-most scored against him. Last week he put up 147.66 and still lost to Tyriese's 166.98. No one has been less rewarded for doing more. Josh Allen is projected for 22.4 and ran in a touchdown last week. Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are the best receiver pair on the field, and Malik Nabers is back from his bye too. His playoff odds are still 80%, because the math knows something the standings don't.
The only time these two have met, Mo won 111.90–82.52 in Week 11 last season. The fans like Mo 6–2, the most lopsided vote of the week.

watch.text: 153 points and the league's best backfield. If he finds the end zone, the belt goes to the Trade God.
Ran one in last week. Mo has scored more than almost anyone; Allen is how he finally gets paid for it.

locker: Zach
Mo can have the points. I'll take the wins. That's how you get a belt.
Mo
I've scored more than everybody and lost to everybody. Somebody's paying for that Sunday, and it's the Trade God.
games.oscarNote: Luck is a fine thing until it runs out, and Zach has been borrowing it all season. Oscar expects Mo to finally climb high enough to collect the debt, and the belt.

games.title: Hogies vs. Marissa: The Hunt
games.lineText: (7–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (−145) vs. (2–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (+120)
games.spreadText: Spread: Hogies −5.5 | Total: 259 | Projection: Hogies 132.4 - Marissa 126.8
story: Hogies is 7–1, has won four straight and sits two games clear in first. Last week he beat Bob with half his team on bye, four waiver pickups and an empty bench. This week the regulars are back: Christian McCaffrey is questionable but projected for 22.9, Chris Olave returns at 15.4, Dak Prescott is projected for 19.8, and Trey McBride and Chuba Hubbard give him two more steady starters. Behind them, though, the bench is held together with tape. Carnell Tate is out, and Romeo Doubs and Jordyn Tyson are on IR. His playoff odds are 99.9%, so this is about keeping the lead, not making the playoffs.

Marissa is 2–6, but she's coming off her best game of the season. She dropped 166.06 on Shmoody last week. She's also been the unluckiest team in the league: 1,127.54 points have been scored against her, the most of anyone. Drake Maye is projected for 21.0 and has run in a touchdown three weeks straight. Tetairoa McMillan is steady, and Patrick Mahomes is projected for 21.2 on her bench, so she may be the only manager with two starting quarterbacks. The problem is her injury report: Saquon Barkley, Travis Kelce, Garrett Wilson, Michael Wilson and Bhayshul Tuten are all questionable. Her playoff odds are 9%, and every win from here is a must.
These two split last season. Hogies won 103.02–93.86 in Week 3, and Marissa won 111.40–96.58 in Week 14. The fans like Hogies 5–2.

watch.text: Questionable. If he plays, the hunter has his biggest weapon back.
Three straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Marissa needs him to keep running.

locker: Hogies
First place, four straight, and the bartenders know my name. Marissa's just another stop on the tour.
Marissa
Everybody's been scoring 160 on me all year. Last week I did it back. Hogies is next.
games.oscarNote: Marissa has the hot hand and two quarterbacks, but Hogies has first place and the habit of winning. Oscar has learned not to bet against a man the bartenders love.

games.title: Tyriese vs. Shmoody: Who Claims the Treasure?
games.lineText: (4–4) Tyriese - No Love in The Land (−125) vs. (1–7) Team Shmoody (+105)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyriese −3 | Total: 269.5 | Projection: Tyriese 136.2 - Shmoody 133.5
story: Two weeks ago, these two were on opposite ends of the first three-team trade in league history. Tyriese gave up Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry and walked away with five starters. Shmoody went the other way, sending out D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins five days after getting them. On Sunday, the trade plays itself out on the same field, and both sides will finally find out who won it.

So far it's been Tyriese. He's 4–4, and last week his new depth beat Mo 166.98–147.66, one of the best scores of the season. Caleb Williams is projected for 18.5, and Swift and Higgins, both from Shmoody, are each projected for 16.6. James Cook adds 15, and Mike Evans is questionable but could be back from injury, projected for 16.4. His playoff odds are 85%, and this is the kind of game that keeps him there.

Shmoody won the whole league last year. Now he's 1–7, has lost three straight and sits alone in last, with playoff odds of 2%. He does have the best player on the field: Puka Nacua is projected for 23.1. Nico Collins adds 17.8, and Henry is still Henry. Kyler Murray is questionable at quarterback, but Bryce Young is right behind him at 17.1. The team is good enough to win; it just hasn't.

Tyriese beat Shmoody 108.80–90.52 in the regular season last year, but Shmoody got the one that mattered. He knocked Tyriese out of the playoffs 162.40–134.30 in the quarterfinals on his way to the title. The fans like Tyriese 7–1.

watch.text: Traded away by Shmoody twice in five days. This is the revenge game.
The prize of the three-team trade and the best projection on the field.

locker: Tyriese
I gave him Puka and he still can't win. The trade's over, and so is his season.
Shmoody
Ask Tyriese what happened in the quarterfinals last year. I end seasons. Ask him about it Sunday.
games.oscarNote: Shmoody has the brightest star on the field and a champion's memory. Tyriese has five starters for every one of Shmoody's. Oscar expects arithmetic to beat nostalgia.

games.title: Bob vs. Collin: Race to the Playoffs
games.lineText: (4–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+245) vs. (5–3) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−305)
games.spreadText: Spread: Bob −20 | Total: 261 | Projection: Bob 140.5 - Collin 120.6
story: Last week Collin was a 17-point underdog against Tim and won 122.36–95.20. This week the sportsbook has made him a 20-point underdog, apparently to see whether he can do it twice. He's won two straight, he's 4–4, and his playoff odds are a coin flip at 49%.

Collin's case starts and ends with Jahmyr Gibbs. Gibbs has scored 195.8 points this season, and at 25.8 he's the highest-projected player in this game. Kirk Cousins is steady at 17.4, and Jameson Williams and Josh Downs, both from his busy trade night, are in the lineup. Behind them it gets thin, and with 1,070.88 points scored against him, Collin has had to beat good scores all year. He's done it the last two weeks.

Bob is 5–3 with playoff odds of 95%, and he's coming off a 101.90–91.14 loss to Hogies with Malik Willis at quarterback. He's done waiting on that: Brock Purdy is in and projected for 22.2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has scored 219.96 points, the most of any receiver in the league, and is projected for 24. Drake London (19.0) and Kyren Williams (18.7) make it the deepest lineup on the field. Deebo Samuel, Denzel Boston and Alvin Kamara are all questionable, but Bob has enough to cover for them.
These two have never played each other. The fans are split 4–4, so the league isn't as sure as the sportsbook.

watch.text: 195.8 points this season and the highest projection on the field.
The league's top-scoring receiver, now with Brock Purdy throwing to him.

locker: Collin
Seventeen points last week, twenty this week. Keep adding points, I'll keep winning.
Bob
Collin got lucky once. I've got JSN and a real quarterback now. Lightning doesn't strike twice.
games.oscarNote: Collin has made a habit of embarrassing the sportsbook, and Oscar admires a good habit. But Bob has the best receiver in the league and finally a quarterback to throw to him. Oscar takes Bob to win, and Collin to cover.

games.title: Sean vs. Tim: The Assassin's Last Job
games.lineText: (6–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−230) vs. (4–4) Tim - The Coffey Shop (+190)
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −15 | Total: 278 | Projection: Sean 146.3 - Tim 131.5
story: Sean has scored 1,138.14 points, the most in the league, and last week he added 139.58 to beat Tyler. Joe Burrow threw five touchdowns, ran in a sixth and put up 39.48. Sean has since called a press conference to demand apologies from everyone who laughed at the trade that brought Burrow over. He's 6–2, and his playoff odds are 99.7%. Now the 2024 champion wants a bye.

The lineup is the most complete in the league. Kenneth Walker is projected for 22.0, Burrow for 21.4, CeeDee Lamb for 20.2 and Jonathan Taylor for 17.5. DJ Moore is questionable, but the bench is deep enough that it doesn't matter. Every one of Sean's big four has scored at least 144 points this season.

Tim is 4–4, has lost two straight and is still recovering from last week, when he lost to Collin as a 17-point favorite. He's since changed his LinkedIn title from "Assassin" to "Assassin (retired)." His playoff odds are 54%, and a third straight loss would put him below .500 for the first time. He does have a lineup that can keep up: Trevor Lawrence is projected for 19.7, and Chase Brown, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are all in the 15-to-16 range. Ashton Jeanty has scored 132.3 points but is projected for only 12.2. Watson and Emeka Egbuka are questionable.
These two have never played each other. The fans are leaning Sean, 4–3.

watch.text: The top projection on the league's best team.
The assassin needs his quarterback to pull the trigger.

locker: Sean
I'm still waiting on those apologies. Tim can go first.
Tim
The assassin's coming out of retirement for one last job. Sean's name is on the list.
games.oscarNote: Every assassin has one last job, but most of them have it planned better than this. Sean has the best team in the league and the patience of a man waiting for an apology. Oscar expects him to get the win instead.

games.title: Tyler vs. Abdo: Get Out of My Swamp!
games.lineText: (3–5) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (−120) vs. (3–5) Abdo - Beat the case (−100)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyler −1.5 | Total: 253 | Projection: Tyler 127.2 - Abdo 125.8
story: This is the closest line of the week, and it's close for a reason. Both are 3–5, both have playoff odds under 15%, and the loser can start planning for the Toilet Bowl. The winner gets to keep pretending.

Tyler has lost three straight, including a 139.58–98.94 loss to Sean last week, and his therapist has reportedly quit after he spent their whole session drawing up a four-team trade on the whiteboard. The three-team trade did give him the core he wanted. Jared Goff is projected for 20.0, Brock Bowers for 18.7 and Javonte Williams for 18.4. Zay Flowers and Ladd McConkey round out the receivers, and Cam Skattebo is questionable. The lineup is good. The record is not.

Abdo has scored 920.58 points, the fewest in the league, and lost 126.28–84.90 to Zach last week. Some of his best players came from Tyler: Bucky Irving is projected for 17.6, and George Pickens is questionable. Jordan Love, last seen suing Abdo for unpaid babysitting wages, is projected for 17.3 at quarterback. A.J. Brown is questionable, and with only 19.1 points since arriving, the bet on his reputation hasn't paid off yet. Josh Jacobs and Tyler Warren give him enough to keep it close.
Their only meeting was last year in Week 8, when Tyler won 140.82–140.28, by 0.54 points. The fans lean Tyler 5–3.

watch.text: Tyler traded three players to get him. Time to earn it.
A former Tyler player, which makes this personal.

locker: Tyler
Abdo's playing my old players. I know exactly how good they are, which is why I traded them.
Abdo
Tyler gave me Bucky and Pickens and he's still trading. Sunday, I give him a reason to stop.
games.oscarNote: Last year these two were separated by half a point, and this year the sportsbook can barely tell them apart. Oscar gives the edge to the man with the better tight end, and urges him to put the whiteboard down.

parlay.headline: Gibbs goes for two
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in. Last week: 8-for-12.
picks: 153 yards and a touchdown last week. Some picks are value plays. This one is just correct.
Everyone will take Bijan. Oscar takes the receiver who put up 23.7 two weeks ago and has quietly become Zach's favorite deep target.
Josh Allen cashed last week. This week the touchdown goes to the receiver, which is how it should have been all along.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba gets the yards. London gets the red zone. With Brock Purdy taking over, Oscar likes the big man in the end zone.
Walker and CeeDee get the headlines. Taylor gets the goal line. Against Tim, there will be plenty of goal line.
Jeanty's projection has gone soft. Golden has the speed to score from anywhere.
Back from his bye and rested. McCaffrey is questionable, so Oscar takes the receiver who's definitely playing.
Three straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Oscar is going for four, because streaks are only interesting until they end.
The team used to be named after him. Now it's called No Love in the Land. Oscar expects the tight end to take that personally.
He cashed last week, and he has never once been stopped at the 1-yard line.
Bowers draws the coverage. Flowers gets loose. Oscar likes the receiver nobody's watching.
Only 19.1 points since arriving. Questionable this week. Oscar is betting on a reputation, which is either brilliant or the dumbest pick on the slip.
parlay.sign: Gibbs is the golden leg again, because he earned it. A.J. Brown is the danger leg, because somebody has to be. Seven receivers, three backs, a tight end and one quarterback with legs. Last week's slip went 8-for-12. This week Oscar is aiming for perfection, which he has never achieved and does not expect to.

cover.headline: Is the second ring on its way?
cover.dek: Sean drops 189.14, the second-highest score of the season, and takes over first place. Mo wins a Monday night Mortal Kombat match, Tyriese beats Shmoody by four hundredths of a point, and Baby Abdo springs his trap on Tyler.
side: Sean and Hogies are both 7–2. Sean has the points, so the 2024 champion is the top seed.
Tyriese beat Shmoody 135.36–135.32. The 0.04 margin breaks the league record by 0.24.
Tyler and Hogies both made trades on Friday. The players they sent away scored 67.40 against them on Sunday, and they both lost.

stories.headline: Get over here! Mo finishes the Trade God with a 3.90-point Fatality
body: All week the Game of the Week was billed as a ladder match for the Smoke Boy Championship. On Sunday it turned into Mortal Kombat, and it went the full three rounds. The sportsbook opened Zach at −4 and closed him at −5.5. The fans liked Mo 6–2, and Oscar picked Mo 143–139. Oscar got the winner. He also predicted fireworks, and the game went **44 points under** the 285 total.

By Sunday night, it looked finished. **Bijan Robinson ran for 100 yards and a touchdown** for **26.70**, a week after going 76 yards without one. **Luther Burden caught 7 for 97 and a touchdown** on Sunday night (20.70), cashing his parlay leg as Oscar's value pick over Bijan. Amon-Ra St. Brown added 16.60. Zach went to bed up **115.36 to 87.70**, a lead of **27.66**, with only Aaron Jones left to play.

Mo had kept his three best fighters for Monday night: **Josh Allen, Justin Jefferson and Tyler Bass** in Bills at Vikings. His Sunday had been carried by **Ja'Marr Chase**, who caught **10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown** (31.50) to cash his parlay leg, plus Rhamondre Stevenson's 14.80 and the Rams D/ST's 15.00. Then the comeback started. Allen threw for 234 yards and a touchdown (12.86), Jefferson added 8.80, and Bass kicked his way to **13.00**. Mo needed 27.66 to catch up. He got **34.66**.

Zach's last fighter didn't show. **Aaron Jones scored 3.10** on Monday night. Meanwhile **Jadarian Price had scored 11.80 on Zach's bench** back on Sunday. Starting Price over Jones would have been worth 8.70 points, and Zach lost by **3.90**. Mo had his own bench mistake, leaving **Isaiah Likely's 16.30** on the bench while Brenton Strange scored 4.20, and he won anyway.
Mo wins by 3.90, moves to **4–5** and takes the belt, and he now leads the series **2–0**. Zach's three-game winning streak is over. He's 6–3, and his luck finally ran out, as Oscar warned it would.
locker: Ja'Marr Chase
Mo said 'Get over here,' so I did. Ten catches, 155 yards. Then I went home and let the Bills finish him.
Oscar
Oscar picked Mo and got the winner. He also promised fireworks and got a Monday night kicker. Oscar has never been so happy to watch a field goal.

stories.headline: Posterized! The Wavy Squad dunks on the Assassin with 189 points
body: Tim came out of retirement for one last job, and Sean dunked on him. The **189.14 is the second-highest score of the season**, behind only Mo's 196.10 record. The sportsbook opened Sean at −15 and closed him at −16. He covered by 31, and the game flew past the 276 total by 55. The fans liked Sean 4–3, and Oscar picked him 145–129.

Four of Sean's players scored over 29. **Kenneth Walker ran for 102 yards, caught 4 passes and scored three touchdowns** for **36.30**. **CeeDee Lamb caught 10 for 195 yards and a touchdown** (33.50). **Joe Burrow threw for 271 and three touchdowns and ran in a fourth** (29.54), so Sean is still waiting on those apologies. Then came the new guys. **Javonte Williams ran for 101 yards and a touchdown** (22.40), and **Brock Bowers caught 7 for 111 and a score** (22.30). Sean got both from Tyler on Friday, two days before kickoff, and they combined for **44.70** in their debut. Oscar has decided not to ask how Tyler feels about it.

Tim wasn't bad. He scored **142.18, the third-highest score of the week**, and lost by 47. His Packers receivers had the best day of their season. **Matthew Golden caught 10 for 164 and a touchdown** (32.40), cashing his parlay leg, and **Christian Watson caught 7 for 171 and a score** (30.10). Spencer Shrader kicked in 16.00. But the rest of the job was botched. **Ashton Jeanty ran for 25 yards and lost 5 receiving** for 7.00, Jaylen Waddle scored 3.20, and Kyle Pitts 5.30.
Sean moves to **7–2**, wins his second straight and stays at the top of the points leaderboard. Tim has lost three straight and, as Oscar warned, has dropped below .500 for the first time at **4–5**.
locker: Kenneth Walker
Three touchdowns. Tim jumped, I jumped higher.
Oscar
Oscar warned that most assassins plan their last job better than this. Tim scored 142 and still got posterized. That's not a botched job, it's a highlight reel.

stories.headline: Follow the yellow brick road: Marissa skips past the heartless Tin Man
body: On Friday, two days before kickoff, Hogies traded **Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to Baby Abdo for Josh Jacobs and George Pickens**. On Sunday, McCaffrey scored **two touchdowns for 22.70** against Tyler. Jacobs ran 5 yards for **0.50**, and Pickens didn't play. Hogies lost by **5.68**. The Tin Man went looking for a heart and gave his away instead.

The sportsbook opened Hogies at −5.5 and closed him at −3, and Marissa won outright. The fans liked Hogies 5–2, and Oscar picked him 133–124, which Oscar would like to take back. The game went **44 points under** the 254 total.

Marissa did it with the quarterback Oscar joked she had two of. She started **Patrick Mahomes**, who threw two touchdowns for **16.48**, while **Drake Maye threw three for 18.26 on her bench**. Maye's run of rushing touchdowns ended at three, which also cost Oscar a parlay leg. **Travis Kelce caught 4 for 72 and ran in a touchdown** (17.30), **Tetairoa McMillan caught a score** (15.60), and Cam Little kicked in 17.00. Saquon Barkley and Bhayshul Tuten each ran one in. She also started Adonai Mitchell, who scored 0.00, while Courtland Sutton's 15.50 sat on the bench. She won anyway.

Hogies didn't have much to work with after the trade. **Dak Prescott threw for 335 and two touchdowns** (19.50), Chris Olave caught 7 for 98 (16.80), and Efton Chism added 15.90 with a touchdown. Then it fell apart. **Mike Washington ran for −3 yards and scored −0.30.** Devin Singletary added 5.90, and Trey McBride was held to 12.40.

Marissa has won two straight and moves to **3–6**, and she's still on the road to the playoffs. Hogies' four-game winning streak is over. He's 7–2, and with Sean also at 7–2 with more points, **Hogies drops to the No. 2 seed.**
locker: Christian McCaffrey
Two touchdowns. Hogies sent me to Abdo and I sent Hogies to second place.
Oscar
Oscar picked Hogies and got the Tin Man. There's no place like first place, and as of Sunday, Hogies doesn't live there anymore.

stories.headline: Look at this noob still in spawn: Sgt. Bob walks right past Collin's claymore
body: Collin did what Collin does. He set up in spawn, planted his claymore, and stared in one direction waiting for Bob to walk into it. Bob came around the other side. The sportsbook opened Bob at −20 and closed him at −18.5, and he covered by 2.84. The fans were split 4–4. Oscar picked Bob 138–124 and said Collin would cover. He didn't, so Oscar got half of that one right.

Collin's claymore went off, but only once. **Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 74 yards and a touchdown** (13.40), cashing the golden leg of Oscar's parlay for a second straight week. **Justice Hill led the team with 18.20** and a touchdown of his own, and Jake Bates kicked in 15.00. Then came the friendly fire. **Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions** and finished with 12.64. **Jameson Williams scored 5.00 and Josh Downs 5.40**, so the two receivers from Collin's big trade night added up to 10.40. Braelon Allen fumbled. Collin's bench had nothing to send in either.

Bob ran his new quarterback right at him. **Brock Purdy threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns and ran in a third** for **25.28** in his first game for Bob, and **the 49ers D/ST added 21.00**. DeMario Douglas caught 5 for 102 (15.20). Bob won comfortably while his stars were quiet. **Jaxon Smith-Njigba was held to 12.10**, and Drake London caught 5 for 68 without the touchdown Oscar's parlay wanted. Bob also left **KC Concepcion's 18.80 and Denzel Boston's 15.80** on his bench. That's 34.60 points he didn't need.
Bob moves to **6–3** and gets back in the race for a bye. Collin's two-game winning streak is over. He's 4–5, still in the hunt, and still in spawn.
locker: Sgt. Bob
I knew exactly where the claymore was. Everybody does. He's been facing that same wall since Week 1.
Collin
I'm not camping. I'm holding a power position.
Oscar
Oscar said Collin would cover. Collin covered his spawn point instead.

stories.headline: Pirate King! Tyriese steals the treasure by 0.04, the closest game in league history
body: The three-team trade rematch came down to **four hundredths of a point**. That's the **closest game in Villains history**, breaking the old record of 0.28 from Marissa's win over Sean in 2025. Shmoody also lost the second-closest, 0.38 to Hogies in Week 3. He's now been on the wrong end of the two closest games the league has ever seen.

The line flipped during the week. Tyriese opened as a 3-point favorite, but by Sunday, Shmoody was favored by 6.5. Tyriese won outright, and the game went over the 266.5 total. The fans liked Tyriese 7–1, and Oscar picked him 137–131. Oscar got the winner.

Shmoody led **126.32 to 118.66** going into Monday night. Each team had one player left in Bills at Vikings. Tyriese had **James Cook**. Shmoody had his kicker, **Will Reichard**. Cook **ran for 107 yards and a touchdown** for **16.70**. Reichard kicked for **9.00**. Tyriese needed 7.66 more than Shmoody on Monday night and got **7.70**.

He got there because of a quarterback decision. Tyriese benched Caleb Williams and started **C.J. Stroud**, who threw for **384 yards and five touchdowns** for **35.36**. Caleb scored 12.76 on the bench. **Tee Higgins**, traded away twice by Shmoody in five days, **caught two touchdowns for 20.20** in the revenge game, and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked in 17.00. It wasn't perfect: D'Andre Swift ran for 31 yards (3.10), and **Tank Dell scored 20.50 on the bench**.

Shmoody did everything but win. **Puka Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown** for **35.00**, the best game on the field. Bryce Young threw three touchdowns (20.34), and Nico Collins caught one (15.50). **Derrick Henry ran for 57 yards and somehow had −3 passing yards** for 5.58, missing his parlay leg. The bench hurt most of all. **Rome Odunze scored 16.00 and Quentin Johnston 13.30**, while Sam LaPorta (7.20) and Woody Marks (8.40) started. Either swap wins the game.
Tyriese wins his second straight and moves to **5–4**. Shmoody has lost four straight and is **1–8**. The champion's ship is sinking.
locker: C.J. Stroud
Five touchdowns and Tyriese still needed a Monday night running back. That's how close this was.
Shmoody
Point zero four. I've been robbed by pirates twice this year.
Oscar
Oscar predicted arithmetic would beat nostalgia. He did not predict the arithmetic would come down to the second decimal.

stories.headline: You've activated my trap card! Baby Abdo sends Tyler to the Shadow Realm
body: On Friday, Abdo set his trap. He sent **Josh Jacobs and George Pickens to Hogies for Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black**. On Sunday, Tyler walked right into it. McCaffrey **scored two touchdowns for 22.70** in his first game for Abdo, and Abdo won by **54.68**. The sportsbook opened Tyler at −1.5 and moved him to −6. The fans liked Tyler 5–3, and Oscar picked him 129–126. Everyone was wrong except Abdo.

Abdo's whole deck came up. **Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran in a fourth** for **36.18**, the best quarterback game of the week. The babysitter finally got paid. **Bucky Irving ran for 97 yards and two touchdowns** (28.50). Bucky came from Tyler, as Oscar pointed out on Thursday, and he played like it. Omar Cooper caught 8 passes (13.80), and the Chiefs D/ST added 13.00. Abdo's **152.98 was the second-highest score of the week**. A.J. Brown didn't play, so Oscar's danger leg lived up to its name.

Tyler made his own move on Friday too. He traded **Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams to Sean for Jonathan Taylor and Jonah Coleman**. On Sunday, Bowers and Javonte scored **44.70 for Sean**. Taylor and Coleman scored **28.20 for Tyler**. Coleman ran one in (18.80), but **Taylor fumbled** and finished with 9.40. **Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and an interception** (5.30), **Zay Flowers caught 3 passes for 6 yards** (5.30), and **Ladd McConkey scored 0.00**. The highest scorer Tyler had left was a rookie running back.
Abdo moves to **4–5** and is back in the race. Tyler has lost four straight and is **3–6**, two games out of a playoff spot with five weeks left. His therapist has declined to comment.
locker: Jordan Love
Four touchdowns. The babysitter's done babysitting.
Tyler
I'll be back from the Shadow Realm. I'm already working on a trade.
Oscar
Oscar urged Tyler to put the whiteboard down. Instead he made another trade, and the trade card was the trap. Oscar has nothing further to add.

news.headline: Mo refuses to take off the belt
news.body: Mo has worn the Smoke Boy Championship belt to work, to the gym and to his nephew's birthday party. He says he'll take it off "when somebody takes it off me." He also left Isaiah Likely's 16.30 on the bench and won anyway, which he's calling "a power move."

news.headline: Zach fires his lineup consultant
news.body: After starting Aaron Jones (3.10) over Jadarian Price (11.80) and losing by 3.90, the Trade God has fired his lineup consultant. The consultant was Zach. He's already offered himself a two-for-one to come back.

news.headline: Sean receives his first apology
news.body: Sean has received his first apology since demanding them last week. It came from Tyler, in the form of Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams, who scored 44.70 for Sean two days later. Sean says the apology "has been accepted, framed and hung in first place."

news.headline: Tim deletes his LinkedIn
news.body: A week after changing his title to "Assassin (retired)," Tim scored 142.18 and still got dunked on by 47. He has deleted his LinkedIn entirely. His Packers receivers, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, combined for 62.50 and have asked to be traded to someone who wins.

news.headline: Bartenders revoke King Hogies' free beer
news.body: After losing first place, Hogies' executive order on complimentary beer has been overturned. Bartenders across the league voted 11–0 to start charging him again. Christian McCaffrey, who Hogies traded on Friday, scored 22.70 and was seen buying a round for Abdo.

news.headline: Drake Maye files a grievance
news.body: Last week Patrick Mahomes complained about the bench. This week Marissa started Mahomes and benched Drake Maye, who threw three touchdowns for 18.26 in the background. Maye has filed a grievance with the league office. Marissa says both quarterbacks "look great from where I'm standing," and right now she's standing on a two-game winning streak.

news.headline: Tyriese upgrades from Giant Slayer to Pirate King
news.body: After winning by 0.04, Tyriese has withdrawn his request to be called "Giant Slayer" and filed to be known as "Pirate King." The league office approved it by four hundredths of a vote. Mo has withdrawn his objection, because he's too busy wearing his belt.

news.headline: Shmoody requests a recount
news.body: Shmoody has lost two games this season by a combined 0.42 points. He's formally requested a recount of Sunday's game and asked whether fantasy points can be rounded. His swimming instructor reports that his ship is now officially underwater.

news.headline: Sgt. Bob uploads the killcam
news.body: Bob has posted the full killcam of his win over Collin to the group chat. It shows Bob walking around Collin's claymore in slow motion. He's also started a sequel to his war memoir: *I Had 34.60 Points on the Bench, Part II*.

news.headline: Collin buys a second claymore
news.body: After losing by 21.34, Collin has bought a second claymore and pointed it at the same wall as the first. Kirk Cousins, whose unemployment claim was denied after he was put back in the lineup, threw three interceptions and has asked to go back on the bench.

news.headline: Jordan Love's lawsuit settles for 36.18
news.body: Jordan Love has dropped his lawsuit for unpaid babysitting wages after Abdo finally started him. Love threw three touchdowns and ran one in for 36.18, the best quarterback score of the week. His lawyer called it "a fair settlement."

news.headline: Tyler's whiteboard confiscated
news.body: After trading Bowers and Javonte to Sean on Friday and losing by 54.68 on Sunday, Tyler has had his whiteboard confiscated by the league office. He's been seen drawing trades on napkins. His former therapist has declined to comment, but she did send Sean a congratulations card.

parlay.headline: Oscar goes 4-for-12
parlay.golden: Golden boy does it again: Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 74 yards and a touchdown, two weeks in a row
parlay.note: Oscar was told to stop picking the best player on every team, so he picked value plays instead. Two of them cashed: Luther Burden and Matthew Golden. The rest of the value went to the players Oscar passed over. Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns after Oscar took Jonathan Taylor, who was then traded to Tyler on Friday and fumbled. Christian McCaffrey scored twice after Oscar took Chris Olave. Bucky Irving scored twice while Oscar's danger leg, A.J. Brown, didn't suit up. Puka Nacua and Bijan Robinson also scored. Drake Maye threw three touchdowns but didn't run one in, so his streak ends at three, and Oscar's quarterback legs fall to 5-for-9 this season.
parlay.sign: Last week Oscar went 8-for-12 picking stars. This week he went 4-for-12 picking value. Oscar has learned that value is just a polite word for wrong. The golden leg remains undefeated, so Oscar will keep riding Gibbs until Gibbs asks him to stop.

rank-2026-9.title: Is the second ring on its way?
rank-2026-9.summary: Sean drops 189 and moves to No. 1. Hogies slips after trading away McCaffrey, Bob climbs two spots with his new quarterback, and Abdo jumps two after springing his trap. Tyler falls to 11th, and Shmoody is still holding up the rest of the league.
rank-2026-9.note: Rank movement is calculated against the published Week 8 Gazette rankings. These are Oscar’s editorial power rankings, not official playoff seeding.

entries.take: The second-highest score of the season, four players over 29, and the top seed on points. He got Bowers and Javonte from Tyler on Friday, and they scored 44.70 on Sunday. The 2024 champion is building toward ring No. 2.
Traded Christian McCaffrey on Friday and watched him score two touchdowns for someone else on Sunday. Lost by 5.68 to a 3–6 team and lost first place with it. Still 7–2, but the crown is off.
Brock Purdy accounted for three touchdowns in his debut, and the 49ers D/ST scored 21. He won comfortably while JSN was held to 12.10, with 34.60 on the bench. That's a team with room to get better.
Won by 0.04, the closest game in league history, with a Monday night running back. C.J. Stroud threw five touchdowns. He has the third-most points in the league and has won two straight.

Lost by 3.90 with 8.70 points on the bench. Bijan and Burden scored, but the bottom of the lineup didn't show up on Monday night. The luck Oscar warned about has run out, and he has the fewest points of any team in the top five.
Won the Game of the Week on a Monday night comeback from 27.66 down. He has the second-most points in the league and is finally being rewarded for it. The record will catch up.
Traded for McCaffrey on Friday, and it was the trap card that sent Tyler to the Shadow Realm. Jordan Love threw for 36.18 and Bucky Irving scored twice. 152.98 was the second-best score of the week.
Gibbs scored again, but Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions, and Collin is still facing the same wall in spawn. He's a coin flip for the playoffs with a claymore for a plan.
Scored 142.18, the third-best score of the week, and lost by 47. He's lost three straight and has fallen below .500. The assassin has retired again, this time from first-half success.
Won two straight, beat the No. 1 team and did it with her backup quarterback on the bench. She's the hottest team in the bottom half.
Four straight losses. Traded Bowers and Javonte on Friday, then lost by 54.68 to a team built partly from his old players. The whiteboard has been confiscated.
Lost by 0.04, which followed a 0.38 loss in Week 3. Puka scored 35, Rome Odunze scored 16 on the bench, and the defending champion's ship is now underwater.

body: Coach Tyler welcomed Jonathan Taylor this week with a full tour of the facility. It took four hours, because Coach stopped at every locker to explain who used to be in it. Brock Bowers’ old locker now has a small framed photo and a candle. In my day, you traded a man and never spoke his name again. Coach spoke it eleven times.

Taylor and rookie Jonah Coleman ran the old-fashioned drills, the kind I respect: tire runs, a blocking sled and a man with a whistle. Coleman hit the sled so hard it moved a full yard, and as a reward Coach let him pick the warm-up music. He picked something with a synthesizer, so Coach played the trombone tape instead. Good man, Coach. Newcomers Juwan Johnson and Joe Milton were issued helmets with no logos, which is how it ought to be.

Ladd McConkey (back, questionable) ran the tire drill off to the side at half speed. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Zonovan Knight (concussion), both out, sat with Jeremiyah Love, Terrance Ferguson and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, all on injured reserve, on what the players now call the bench of broken toys. They heckled the tour. I joined them.
reports.headline: Coach Tyler gives Jonathan Taylor a facility tour, and it takes four hours

quote.text: And this is where Brock used to tape his ankles.

body: Hey guys, welcome back to the channel! Today’s vlog is a little different, because Coach Collin did not leave the tunnel. Like, at all. He set up at the locker room door, planted a claymore at the 20-yard line (it’s a prop, relax) and crouched behind a Gatorade cooler staring at it for two straight hours. Nobody went near the 20. The whole practice happened between the 21 and the end zone. Smash that like button!

Meanwhile, the waiver wire kept walking in. Mike Gesicki, Michael Mayer, Isaiah Davis, Chimere Dike and kicker Cairo Santos all showed up this week and had to introduce themselves to each other, because Coach was still at the door. Justice Hill ran the welcome tour wearing a sash that said “Breakout.” Jahmyr Gibbs and Jake Bates ran the same fake punt eleven times, yelling “COACH, YOU CAN COME OUT NOW.” He did not come out.
Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring, injured reserve) watched from the side field and was the only person allowed near Coach, since he was already hurt. Link in bio!
reports.headline: Vlog: Coach Collin runs practice from the tunnel, plants a claymore and does not blink for two hours

body: PEOPLE. PEOPLE. Coach seanwavy showed up to his first practice as the No. 1 seed carrying a gold throne and set it down on the 50-yard line. Then he announced that the fog machine is retired with full honors. It has its own locker now. It has a nameplate. I teared up.

The new arrivals, Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams, got the welcome treatment: they carried the throne from drill to drill while the speakers played a boxing ring announcer’s intro on loop. Kenneth Walker III and CeeDee Lamb ran the “victory lap” drill, which is one lap, very slowly, waving. CeeDee waved at the parking lot. The parking lot waved back. ABSOLUTE SCENES.
Brandon Aiyuk (knee) signed his paperwork on the side field and got the best seat in the house: the throne. Coach made him get up after four minutes.
reports.headline: Coach seanwavy puts a gold throne on the 50 and makes the new guys carry it

quote.text: It’s a Tuesday. Why is there a ring announcer?

body: Name’s Rocco Kowalski, 31 years in the trades. They sent me to cover this outfit because the last reporter showed up in a tiara. Good call. Coach Hogies runs practice like a job site: whistle at 6:58, coffee break at nine sharp, and the whole crew built a new goalpost by hand before lunch. Measured twice, cut once. Level. Plumb. I’ve seen worse work from guys charging triple.

Dak Prescott and Chris Olave ran routes around the sawhorses, and every receiver had to read a tape measure out loud on the way back to the huddle. Backup quarterback Tyler Shough threw the best balls of the morning and got a handshake and a cold one after work. On this crew, that’s a promotion. New guys Josh Jacobs and George Pickens got their tool belts and steel toes on day one.

Light duty on the side field: Jacobs (finger), Pickens (hamstring), David Montgomery (groin) and Carnell Tate (shoulder), all out, sanded two-by-fours, and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, injured reserve) ran the time sheet. At four o’clock everybody clocked out and headed to the bar. First round was on Coach. Good man.
reports.headline: Coach Hogies runs a tight job site: whistle at 6:58, coffee at nine, new goalpost by lunch

quote.text: Measure twice, cut once, block your man.

body: Practice was open today, which is the most suspicious thing that has happened all season. An open practice means they WANT me to see something, so I watched everything. C.J. Stroud threw for two hours straight and never once looked at the sideline. A man with nothing to hide looks at the sideline. Coach Tyriese had the smooth jazz on again, louder this time, which is exactly how you cover the sound of a paper shredder.

Then I saw it. Tank Dell, a bench player, was running with the first team. Nobody announced it. Nobody explained it. When I asked, a team spokesman said, “He’s been on the roster all year.” Has he? Has he, though? The corkboard has a new section labeled DELL, with four strings and a question mark I drew so hard it tore the paper. Tee Higgins was spotted winking again. Same wink, different angle.

Mike Evans (Achilles) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring), both listed out, did their rehab off to the side behind a portable curtain. A curtain. Davante Adams (hamstring, injured reserve) was there too. Or someone wearing his jersey was.
reports.headline: Tank Dell is practicing with the starters. Nobody will say why. I have theories.

quote.text: It’s an open practice. You can just walk in. Please stop crawling.

body: After weeks in the parking lot, I finally got inside. I put on a jersey, grabbed a duffel bag and walked in behind this week’s free-agent signings, Samaje Perine and Demarcus Robinson. Nobody stopped me. Nobody even looked up. The congregation had bigger problems: the Trade God hasn’t made a trade in almost three weeks.

Coach Zach paced the sideline, refreshing the trade block on two phones while the speakers played a slowed-down Sleeper notification sound on loop. Every time it chimed, the whole roster froze. Bijan Robinson scored on every rep without anyone noticing, which the followers called “a sign.” Perine was handed a playbook and told not to get attached to it.

Luther Burden (undisclosed, questionable) did his reps on the side field and kept looking over his shoulder, as players here do. TreVeyon Henderson (illness, out) stayed home again and has been added to the prayer list. I was discovered at the snack table and escorted back to my car.
reports.headline: Undercover: your reporter sneaks in with the free agents and finds the Trade God in withdrawal

quote.text: Someone gets traded tonight. It might be me. It might be the coach.

body: What a Tuesday! Coach Marissa declared it Gratitude Day. Every player wrote a thank-you card to a teammate before stretches, and the speakers played only songs with “sunshine” in the title. There are more of those than you’d think. Seventeen at last count!

Travis Kelce got a card from every player on the roster, plus one from the long snapper’s mom, who was visiting. He read them all aloud. It took most of practice, and nobody minded! Cam Little kicked field goals between cards and made every one. New receiver Darius Cooper got a welcome card the size of a door. Drake Maye wrote “thanks for having me” on his and signed it “your backup, for now :)”.

Patrick Mahomes (elbow, questionable) wrote his cards left-handed off to the side. Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Rashid Shaheed (knee), both out, had their cards read to them softly in the shade. Michael Wilson (neck) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen), on injured reserve, got a fruit basket. Still the best mood in the league!
reports.headline: Marissa’s team holds Gratitude Day, and Travis Kelce gets a thank-you card from everyone

quote.text: Gratitude is free, and so was Darius Cooper!

body: Tuesday rating: four beans out of five, a season high. Coach Tim unveiled a new house blend on the menu board, the Golden-Watson, a double shot so strong the espresso machine had to sit down after the second pour. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson wore aprons and served it to the whole roster themselves. Watson is finally off decaf. The routes were crisp. The foam was crisp. Everything was crisp.

Then a small disaster. Coach Tim brought kicker Spencer Shrader behind the counter to demonstrate the perfect tamp, and Shrader tamped so hard the portafilter flew straight through the uprights. Thirty-nine yards. Good. Coach called it the best kick of the day and docked one bean for the mess.
Jaylen Waddle (head, out) spent the session in the café’s quiet corner with a chamomile and the lights dimmed, which is exactly the right order for that situation. Austin Ekeler wiped down tables.
reports.headline: The Coffey Shop scores a season-high four beans, thanks to the Golden-Watson house blend

quote.text: We’re out of oat milk. We’re out of everything. They drank the whole menu.

body: Today was a landmark session. For the first time this season, Coach Bob turned his attention to defense, specifically the 49ers defense, which he owns. He made the entire offense study it frame by frame. Nobody on this offense will ever play against the 49ers defense in this league. Coach said that is exactly why they must understand it.

Brock Purdy was brought to the front of the room so the group could study his release in slow motion, at one-sixteenth speed, with a cello playing underneath. One throw took eleven minutes to watch. Purdy called it “a lot of looking at myself.” KC Concepcion, who had a big week from the bench, was shown film of the bench itself, so he could understand where he was and why.

Concepcion (leg, questionable) watched the bench film from a bench on the side field, which Coach called “immersive.” Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and MarShawn Lloyd (knee), both out, kept their recliners. Travis Etienne (hamstring, injured reserve) asked for the film to be emailed.
reports.headline: Coach Bob turns film study to his own defense, which no one on the roster will ever face

quote.text: Pause it. Look at the bench. Do you see the bench?

body: Christian McCaffrey reported at seven. Coach Abdo shook his hand, pointed at the field and turned the metal back up. That was orientation.
Jordan Love threw for an hour, and Bucky Irving ran it back every time. Shedeur Sanders, also new, asked where the quarterback room was. He was told “there” and handed a clipboard.

Side field: Lamar Jackson (thumb), Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) and RJ Harvey (knee) are on injured reserve, and Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and A.J. Brown (knee) are out. Nobody talked there either. I went home.
reports.headline: McCaffrey showed up. Love threw. Nobody talked.

body: Big news from the snack table: Coach Shmoody hired a hibachi chef and set the grill up right on the sideline. Ten out of ten. The onion volcano alone was worth the drive. Football also happened, nearby.

The chef got involved. Every time a receiver ran past, he flipped a shrimp, and you had to catch it in your mouth before you could run your route. Bryce Young threw with a spatula in his back pocket, just in case. Rome Odunze, moving up to No. 1 receiver, caught nine straight and got the first plate. New arrival Quentin Johnston dropped his first shrimp and was sent to the back of the line, which is the hibachi way.

Puka Nacua (knee and toe, injured reserve) caught eleven straight shrimp from a recliner on the side field without ever leaving the chair. The chef called them the best hands he’s ever seen. Kyle Monangai (toe, out) ate beside him, and James Conner (foot, injured reserve) ordered extra yum yum sauce. Ten out of ten again.
reports.headline: Shmoody hires a hibachi chef, and the shrimp-catching drill is born

quote.text: We’re close. I can feel it. Pass the yum yum sauce.

body: WELCOME BACK, FOLKS, to a Tuesday that felt like the final drive of the Super Bowl! Coach Mohammed hauled a full-size game clock onto the field, set it to 2:00 and ran the two-minute drill for the next two hours. Every time the clock hit zero, he reset it and yelled “SAME SITUATION!” The air horns, I can report, have been confiscated by the homeowners’ association.

And here comes Ja’Marr Chase on a go route into three assistants holding pool noodles. He’s got a step, he’s got TWO steps, the ball is in the air… CAUGHT! Chase spiked it, picked it up and spiked it again for the folks in the back row. Coach Mo handed him the game ball. It was the only ball. Practice was delayed eight minutes.

On the side field, Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and Jake Ferguson (knee), both out, called the action from folding chairs into a microphone that wasn’t plugged in. Jonathon Brooks (abdomen) and Alec Pierce (heel), on injured reserve, ran the clock. They ran it badly. It still read 2:00 when I left.
reports.headline: AND THE CROWD GOES WILD: Mo runs the two-minute drill for two straight hours

quote.text: Sir, the HOA has asked me to take the backup air horns too.
